recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source edit is needed for FHIR-13684; future readability or regex-portability changes should proceed under a current-version tracker rather than reopening the STU3 year-zero correction.
issue_request: FHIR-13684 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core datatypes issue reporting that date and dateTime regexes allowed year 0000 and day 00 values such as 0000-01-00. The resolution was to replace the four-digit year component with a non-zero-year expression for date and the leading date portion of dateTime, and align validator behavior.
initial_application: Git-svn commit f2b3f28b2ff336fda895e176b2bdb2690ade688b explicitly applied #13684 together with #13685, replacing the old `-?[0-9]{4}` year component with the current non-zero-year expression in source/datatypes/primitives.xml. The Jira comment records svn revision 12460, matching that commit.
additional_context: source/datatypes/primitives.xml is the current primitive datatype source for the regex surface rendered by source/datatypes.html, with primitive pages routed through source/fhir.ini. Historical release artifacts show the old regex in release3 and the corrected expression in release4 and later. FHIR-52866 later proposed a look-ahead simplification of the same year expression, but was resolved No Change because FHIR keeps these regexes within widely supported constructs.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current date and dateTime regexes reject 0000, 0000-01, 0000-01-00, and 9999-12-00 while accepting ordinary partial/full dates; the narrative still says dates SHALL be valid dates for calendar validity beyond what the informative regex enforces.
